html:
South Africa has had the largest number of people living with HIV of any country, with millions infected since the epidemic spread in the 1990s.

Migrant labour, poverty and the upheavals of the end of apartheid helped the virus spread. Under President Thabo Mbeki, from 1999 to 2008, the government questioned whether HIV caused AIDS and delayed giving antiretroviral drugs. A Harvard study later estimated that over 300,000 deaths could have been prevented.

The Treatment Action Campaign took the government to court and won an order in 2002 to provide drugs to prevent mother-to-child infection. From the late 2000s the country built the world's largest treatment programme, and life expectancy recovered. It is the largest chapter of the AIDS epidemic, like Eswatini next door.
sum: South Africa has had the largest number of people living with HIV of any country, with millions infected since the epidemic spread in the 1990s.
